features.description: Operator-editable caps file at ~/.jarvis/quota_caps.json. Schema: {schema_version: 1, defaults: {claude_tier}, <vendor>: {<tier>: {<window>: {cap, unit, _note?}}}}. NOT in repo (lives in ~/.jarvis/, outside the tree). NOT reusing dashboard/state/costs.json (different audience: app-level GCP $-spend vs per-vendor agent quota — see feedback_operator_config_separation.md). Sibling subcommands on `python -m jarvis_orchestrate`: `quota-caps init [--overwrite]` writes a starter file (samples current Codex rolling_5h via _codex_usage_v2 to derive cap = ceil(observed * 1.25); falls back to high provisional 1B tokens if no sample; refuses to overwrite without flag); `quota-caps show` reads + validates the file and prints effective caps. Starter caps: claude.max_20x rolling_7d/rolling_5h cap=100 unit=percent_of_plan with _note flagging the F006 uncalibrated-skip requirement; codex.plus.rolling_5h unit=tokens_local_proxy (NOT messages_estimate — F006 compares against observed_native which is tokens, so messages_estimate would silently false-trip); gemini.code_assist_individuals.rolling_24h cap=1000 unit=requests; grok={} (empty until F003 detects a real signal). Loader validates schema_version + KNOWN_VENDORS/TIERS/WINDOWS/UNITS at load-time; rejects unknowns with named-key errors. Permits underscore-prefixed keys (_note, _owner) so operators can comment inline. defaults.claude_tier informs _detect_claude_tier (F003) so the cap-key tier and the v2 vendors{} block tier match without a separate config.

features.description: Claude calibration command + sticky storage. CLI: `python -m jarvis_orchestrate calibrate-claude --dashboard-pct N [--window rolling_7d|rolling_5h]` (default rolling_7d). Reads observed_native for the named window from current ~/.jarvis/quota_state.json. Computes ratio = dashboard_pct / observed_native. Writes the calibration to a SEPARATE sticky file at ~/.jarvis/quota_calibration.json (NOT in-place mutation of quota_state.json — that file is generated state, overwritten on every quota_check.py refresh; calibration is operator configuration that must survive refreshes). Sticky shape: {schema_version: 1, claude: {<window>: {ratio, confidence:'manual', source:'operator_dashboard_sample', dashboard_pct, observed_native, stamped_at}}}. quota_check._build_state lazy-imports calibration_loader.load() (fail-soft, returns {} on any missing/malformed input) and merges matching block into vendors.claude.windows.<window>.calibration via get_for_window which projects to the breaker shape (ratio/confidence/source/stamped_at — drops dashboard_pct + observed_native operator-input metadata). When no sticky entry exists, the uncalibrated default block (ratio:null, confidence:'uncalibrated', source:null, stamped_at:null) is preserved. Confidence levels: uncalibrated (default), manual (this command's output), auto (RESERVED — never set automatically; would require a vendor API that does not exist for the consumer Max plan). Guardrails: dashboard_pct must be in (0, 100], observed_native must be positive (rejects zero), --window restricted to {rolling_7d, rolling_5h} (Claude has no 24h window). quota_check.py main() emits stderr warning when any Claude calibration is older than 7 days (STALE_WARNING_DAYS); operator owns re-cal cadence. Aged calibration still applies (no auto-revert) — warning prompts re-sample.

features.description: Breaker rewrite in scripts/jarvis_orchestrate/circuit_breakers.py + migration of three sibling orchestrator-side consumers (supervisor._quota_gate, quota_admission, signoff_writer) per the rg consumer scan in F002. check_budget_ceiling(plan, agent): for each window in state.vendors[agent].windows, look up cap+unit via quota_caps_loader.get(vendor, tier, window); compute (observed_native * (calibration.ratio or 1.0)) / cap; trip if any window > 1.0. CRITICAL CALIBRATION-SAFETY RULE: when the window has a calibration block AND calibration.confidence == 'uncalibrated', SKIP the budget_ceiling check for that window and emit an INBOX `calibration_required` event with body pointing operators at `python -m jarvis_orchestrate calibrate-claude --dashboard-pct N` (F005). This prevents Claude weighted_tokens_local_proxy values (hundreds of millions) from false-tripping against percent_of_plan caps (max 100) before F005 calibration runs. INBOX 'breaker_tripped' wording surfaces (a) which window tripped, (b) tier, (c) observed vs cap, (d) calibration confidence label. Backward-compat fallback: if state.vendors block missing (legacy state shape), use old models{}.percent_weekly path with a single-shot deprecation log. Plan-level quota_caps field still consulted as a per-plan override IF present (most plans now omit per D010); else fall back to operator caps file as source of truth. Plan 004's original D001 ('which of three semantics') is answered structurally: per-vendor per-window absolute usage ceiling, semantic (1) generalized. Three sibling consumers also migrate in this slice: supervisor._quota_gate(agent) reads vendors{}.<agent>.windows for soft-warn at >=90% (autonomous tier), prefer rolling_5h primary; quota_admission.QuotaCheck reads vendors{} for defer:quota_threshold; signoff_writer summarizes per-vendor per-window observed values instead of flat percent_weekly. All three keep the legacy models{} fallback path active (writer-side mirror still emits per F002 D011 mirror policy).
